text:
alex: ran a long nsys capture against ded-prod-12 during the latency spike. seeing a cascade of JIT compiles after several KV-cache misses — tail latency shot up when the first few requests hit new kernel shapes. attaching perfetto link and short logs below.

maria: perfetto: https://perfetto/trace/abcd1234 (nsys -> perfetto export). quick glance shows repeated compile tasks at ~50ms each clustered in a 1s window. :grimacing:

cheng: pasted snippet from nsys timeline:
```
[12:04:17.102] triton_jit_compiler::compile_kernel (shape=H:128,S:512) -> 52.3ms
[12:04:17.160] triton_jit_compiler::compile_kernel (shape=H:128,S:384) -> 48.7ms
[12:04:17.214] triton::matmul_fallback -> 27.9ms
[12:04:17.252] aten::kernel_launch shape=... -> 31.1ms
```
several of those happen back-to-back and block the serving thread.

jordan: hypothesis: batching mixes seq-lens and forces the runtime to pick multiple new kernel variants within the same batch interval. when KV cache is cold or evicted we also waste time rebuilding KV-friendly kernels.

infra-bot: noticed instance rotation on ded-prod-12 at 12:03:58 (auto-redeploy). new worker started with empty kernel cache.

cheng: key observation: the compile churn aligns to the worker startup + a short burst of long sequences (~>384) from a small subset of tenants. once the per-worker kernel cache fills with those shapes, latency returns to normal. so this is warmup + eviction + shape diversity problem.

maria: repro plan: run a synthetic burst that mixes short/long sequences to reproduce compile cascade. script to use: `./tests/loadgen.sh --model redwood-2b --seq-dist "[32:0.8,512:0.2]" --rate 200`. will run against canary pool.

alex: candidates to try: 1) persist kernel cache across worker restarts (disk-backed cache) 2) prewarm common shapes on startup based on recent workload profile 3) change batcher to avoid co-batching extreme seq-len within same microbatch (prefer homogeneous microbatches) 4) add quick fallback: if compile backlog > N, route to a slightly older but precompiled kernel variant to avoid tail spike.

jordan: i can prototype batcher change. quick tweak: split microbatching by quantized seq-length bins (32/128/384/512) and cap cross-bin mixing. should limit new-shape surface.

cheng: also noticed Triton falls back to `matmul_fallback` for some head counts (H mod 32 != 0) which increases compile frequency. we should add a kernel-selector rule: prefer precompiled fallback kernels for those head counts until a compiled optimized variant exists.

maria: i'll run the loadgen in canary and attach nvprof/nsys flame slices. expect to reproduce within ~15m. assigning: cheng -> perfetto deep-dive + recommend shape list; jordan -> batcher patch prototype; alex -> kernel-cache persistence spike test. target: ship quick mitigations to canary by EOD. :rocket:

cheng: quick note after a 10m sample: the top hotpaths during cascade are `triton::jit_compile`, `cudaLaunchKernel` stalls, and CPU-side `kernel_selector::choose`. compile queue peaked at ~18 concurrent compile tasks which matches the JIT worker pool size. reducing pool or serializing compile doesn't solve latency but serializing reduces CPU churn.

alex: perfect. keep updates here. if anyone finds a small config to disable JIT for shapes >512 temporarily, post it and we'll flip in canary.

maria: +1. will post perf graphs and nvprof slices once done.
